title: Now Hiring: Sidekick
text:
Now hiring! Captain Kindness is looking for a {adjective} sidekick to help around town. You will work every Saturday from nine until lunchtime.

Your jobs will include helping kittens down from trees, carrying groceries for neighbors, and finding lost {plural noun}. You must be able to run {adverb}, hop over a {noun}, and {verb} without getting dizzy. You must not be afraid of {plural noun}.

Every sidekick gets a cape, a mask, and a bright {color} belt with {number} pockets. Captain Kindness will also teach you the secret hero handshake. It uses your {body part} and a little bit of {verb ending in ing}. Sidekicks may not {verb} in the hero car.

Our last sidekick {past tense verb} so much that he needed a long vacation. To apply, please bring a smile, a pencil, and a {adjective} sandwich to the library on Tuesday.

title: My First Week with Super Powers
text:
Dear Diary,
On Monday I woke up and found out I have super powers! I can fly, but only about as high as a {noun}. I can also see through walls, but only if I wiggle my {body part} first.

On Tuesday I used my powers for good. I helped Mrs. Kim find her {adjective} glasses. They were on top of her {body part} the whole time. Then I flew to the park and {past tense verb} with the ducks. The ducks were very {adjective} about it.

On Wednesday I tried to {verb} faster than a train. I went so fast that my socks flew off and landed in a pile of {plural noun}. Mom says superheroes still have to pick up their socks.

Today I made my own cape out of a blanket and {number} {plural noun}. My super name is Captain {silly word}. Tomorrow I will practice {verb ending in ing} and flying {adverb} at the same time.

title: Rules at Superhero Headquarters
text:
Welcome to Superhero Headquarters! Please read these rules before you put on your cape.

Rule one: No flying in the hallways. Last week Thunder Girl flew into a {noun} and tipped over the lemonade. Rule two: Hang your cape on a hook, not on the {plural noun}. Rule three: Please do not {verb} on the new carpet in muddy boots.

Rule four: The kitchen is for snacks only. Our cook, Mr. Fox, makes a {adjective} sandwich with cheese and {plural noun}. Please eat it {adverb}, and do not use your heat vision to warm it up. Rule five: Use super strength only for {adjective} jobs, like lifting a {noun} or opening a jar of {plural noun}.

Rule six: When the hero phone rings, answer it right away. Someone may need help finding a lost {animal} or carrying {number} heavy bags. Every hero must be ready to go, even while {verb ending in ing}. Thank you, and have a {adjective} day of helping!

title: Local Hero Rescues Kitten Again
text:
Good morning, this is Radio Ten news. For the third time this week, the hero known as Zoom Girl has rescued a kitten named Muffin from the big oak tree on Pine Street.

Neighbors say Muffin climbs the tree every morning to look at the {plural noun}. Then she gets nervous and meows {adverb} until help arrives. Today, Zoom Girl flew up, lifted Muffin out of a {adjective} nest, and {past tense verb} back down to the sidewalk.

"Muffin is a good kitten," Zoom Girl told our reporter. "She just likes to {verb} in high places." Muffin's owner, Mr. Lee, thanked Zoom Girl with a hug and {number} plates of {food}.

Next week, the town will put a soft {noun} at the bottom of the tree. Zoom Girl will keep {verb ending in ing} until Muffin learns to climb down by herself. In other news, a parade of {plural noun} is coming to {place} on Saturday. Stay {adjective}, everyone!

title: Breakfast of Heroes
text:
Every superhero needs a good breakfast before a long day of helping. This is the famous Hero Smoothie that Captain Comet drinks every morning.

First, put two bananas and a cup of milk into the {adjective} blender. Next, add a big handful of {plural noun} and one {adjective} {noun}. For flying power, add a spoonful of {plural noun}.

Now blend it {adverb} for {number} seconds. If the blender begins to {verb}, that is normal. If it {past tense verb} off the counter, try again tomorrow. Pour the smoothie into your tallest cup and top it with a sprinkle of {plural noun}.

Drink it all in one sip while {verb ending in ing} on one foot. Captain Comet says it tastes a lot like {food}. Then wash your cup, put on your cape, and go have a {adjective} day!

title: Meet Captain Helpful
text:
This month, our class got to interview Captain Helpful, the friendliest hero in town. He came to our classroom in a {color} cape and sat in Ms. Gray's chair.

First, we asked how he got his powers. "I ate a {adjective} sandwich at the library," he said. "The next morning, I could lift {number} {plural noun} with one finger." Then we asked about his favorite power. "Flying," he said. "But I also like to {verb} really fast."

Next, we asked about his best rescue ever. He said a little boy once lost his {noun} at the park. Captain Helpful searched {adverb} for three hours and finally found it under a {adjective} slide.

Last, we asked how kids can be heroes. "Be kind, share your {plural noun}, and help your family," he said. "Eat your carrots and your {plural noun}. And never stop {verb ending in ing}." Then he gave us each a {noun}, waved, and {past tense verb} out the door.

title: Letter Home from Hero Camp
text:
Dear Grandma,
Hero camp is the best place ever! My cabin is called Blue Lightning. It has {number} bunk beds and a {adjective} flag. My camp leader, Captain Sunny, is very {adjective} and can fly backwards.

Every morning we practice our powers. Yesterday I lifted a {noun} over my head. My friend Leo practiced being invisible, but we could still see his {body part}. In the afternoon we learned how to {verb} on the soft grass.

At dinner we eat hero stew, which is mostly carrots and {plural noun}. Then we sit by the campfire and sing songs about {plural noun}. Captain Sunny sings {adverb}. Last night I {past tense verb} so hard that I fell asleep before the song ended.

I will be home on Sunday. Please save me a slice of {food} and tell the dog I have been {verb ending in ing} every day.
Love,
Ava

title: How to Design Your Own Cape
text:
Every hero needs a good cape. Here is how to make your very own.

First, find an old towel or blanket. Ask a grown-up first! Lay it flat on the floor and decorate it with markers, stickers, and {plural noun}. Many heroes draw a big {noun} in the middle. That is your hero symbol.

Next, choose your hero colors. Most heroes pick red or blue, but you can pick {color}. Then give yourself a hero name, like Captain {silly word} or The {adjective} Wonder. Ask your grown-up to clip the cape to your shirt with a {noun}.

Now practice your hero moves. Stand tall, put your hands on your {plural noun}, and get ready to {verb}. A real hero walks {adverb} and helps anyone who is {verb ending in ing}. Last week, a hero named Kim {past tense verb} so fast that her cape flew off. Your cape may feel {adjective} at first. When you are done, hang it next to your {plural noun} so it is ready for tomorrow.

title: Superhero Talent Show Tonight
text:
Attention, everyone! The yearly Superhero Talent Show starts tonight at six o'clock in the town park. Bring a blanket, a snack, and your {adjective} family.

Twelve heroes will show off their powers. Rocket Ron will fly in circles while holding a {noun}. Ice Lady will make a snowman shaped like a {animal}. Mighty Max will lift {number} {plural noun} at the same time, and then he will {verb} for the crowd.

The judges are Mayor Bell, a librarian, and a very {adjective} dog named Scout. Scout will bark {adverb} when he likes an act. The winner gets a golden cape and a whole year of free {plural noun}.

The snack table will have popcorn, apples, and {food}. Please clap {adverb}, cheer kindly, and do not try {verb ending in ing} on the stage. Last year a hero did that, and the stage {past tense verb} for an hour.

title: Postcard from a Hero on Vacation
text:
Dear Sidekick,
Greetings from Sunny Beach! Even heroes need a vacation. I am staying in a little hotel shaped like a {noun}, and every morning I eat pancakes with {plural noun} on top.

I am trying very hard to relax, but it is not easy. Yesterday a beach ball floated away, so I {past tense verb} into the waves and brought it back. Then a little boy dropped his ice cream, so I flew {adverb} to the shop and got him a {adjective} new one. Today I helped a {adjective} crab carry {number} {plural noun} home.

Tomorrow I plan to {verb} in the sand all day and not rescue anything at all. I brought a towel and a {adjective} book about {plural noun}. Please water my plants and feed my {animal} while I am gone.
See you soon,
Captain Starlight
P.S. I got sand in my {body part}.
